intro.title: About Place of Silence – Hallstatt
intro.description: Place of Silence is a lakeside location in Hallstatt, distinct from the Skywalk above the town.
intro.nearbyText: Hallstatt is a lived-in town as well as a cultural landscape. Its homes, streets and daily routines deserve consideration. Consult the regional tourism portal for general town information rather than treating this residential location as a required stop.

visitGuide.title: Visiting Tips
items: Keep voices low and respect the quiet character of this residential setting.
Keep paths, roads and doorways clear. If space is crowded, continue on rather than forming a queue.
Do not enter private gardens or photograph residents through windows.
Follow current signs and traffic instructions. Do not arrive at dawn or late at night simply to obtain an empty photograph.

alsoKnownAs.title: Name & Local Context
items: Older references may call it Viewpoint or Aussichtspunkt Hallstatt; those names are retained here only for identification.
The lakeside surroundings include private homes and ordinary local traffic.
The name update is not evidence of a new legal access ban or approval of this website.

sections.title: World Heritage
sections.content: The viewpoint looks out over the Hallstatt-Dachstein/Salzkammergut Cultural Landscape, inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1997. The settlement sits on one of Europe's oldest salt-trading routes, with 7,000 years of mining history beneath the surrounding mountains.

sections.title: Traditional Architecture
sections.content: From the northern shore you see Hallstatt's timber-fronted houses climbing the mountainside, crowned by the spire of the Evangelical Parish Church. The compact old town is car-free, with painted facades and narrow lanes that are part of the protected heritage ensemble.

sections.title: A Living Lakeside Setting
sections.content: Weather and seasons change the lakeside landscape, but residents’ privacy and quiet remain important throughout the year. This page does not recommend particular photography times or encourage crowds at this location.

sections.title: Salt, Name & Prehistory
sections.content: Hallstatt takes its name from the Old High German word 'hall' meaning salt – for centuries the 'white gold' of the region. After graves were discovered in 1846 in the high valley above the town, archaeologists named Europe's oldest Iron Age culture after this site: the Hallstatt culture (c. 800–450 BC).

hours.title: Opening Hours
hours.outdoorTime: Follow on-site signs and any current local restrictions; no all-hours access guarantee is made here.
hours.summerTime: Open all day; boat and ferry tours run seasonally
hours.winterTime: Open daily, hours vary by season (usually 09:30-16:30); check the official website
hours.warningTime: The viewpoint stands directly beside the busy lakeside road. Keep off the carriageway, watch for traffic, never block residents' driveways, and do not fly drones over private property.
hours.tip: This is a residential setting, not a scheduled photo attraction. Avoid disturbing residents at any time, especially early in the morning and at night.

tickets.cardPrice: For travel to Hallstatt, consult current regional transport information. Do not plan a separate photography stop at Place of Silence.

transport.title: Transportation
transport.airportDesc: The nearest airports are Salzburg Airport (SZG), about 80 km / 1.5 hours by road, and Vienna International Airport (VIE), about 290 km / 3.5 hours. From either airport, take a train to Hallstatt via Attnang-Puchheim or Bad Ischl.
transport.selfDriveDesc: Use Hallstatt’s designated visitor parking and check current municipal access arrangements. Do not stop on the lakeside road or use residents’ entrances as parking or drop-off space.
transport.busDesc: For travel to Hallstatt, check current rail, bus and ferry connections with the operators and regional tourism office. Timetables, interchange points and service availability can change; the map here is for identification, not a dedicated photo-stop itinerary.
transport.intercityDesc: Obertraun on the far shore is a good base: park there and cross to Hallstatt by ferry or local bus to avoid the busy parking lots in peak season.
transport.cyclingDesc: The lakeside roads around Hallstatt are popular with cyclists. Once you enter the town, dismount and push your bike, as lanes are narrow and crowded with pedestrians.
transport.tipsDesc: Use the linked map only to identify the place. Do not use queues or groups of photographers as directions, and do not obstruct roads or residents’ access.

route.title: Moving Through Hallstatt Respectfully
route.overview: Practical conduct, not a photo-stop itinerary
steps: Check current municipal and transport information before travelling to Hallstatt.
Use designated public routes and follow local traffic instructions.
Keep doorways, gardens and residential entrances clear.
If passing Place of Silence, keep voices low and avoid forming a photography queue.
If the roadside space is crowded, continue on safely rather than waiting in the carriageway.
Use the regional tourism office for broader town information and current opening arrangements.
supplements: Do not step into the carriageway to obtain a view or photograph.
Respect private homes, gardens and residents’ daily routines.

hotels.title: Accommodation & Dining

hotels.name: Lakeside Guesthouses in Hallstatt
hotels.desc: Historic timber guesthouses in the centre offer an unforgettable stay above the lake - book months ahead for summer.
hotels.price: Very limited and expensive in peak season

hotels.name: Obertraun (opposite shore)
hotels.desc: A quiet, well-priced base across the lake, connected to Hallstatt by ferry and local bus.
hotels.price: Best-value alternative when Hallstatt is full

hotels.name: Bad Ischl (the Salzkammergut hub)
hotels.desc: The elegant spa town where the train from Salzburg stops, about 30-40 minutes from Hallstatt by train and bus.

hotels.supplementsContent: Around the lake, restaurants serve freshly caught fish from the Hallstätter See, such as grilled Reinanke, alongside Austrian classics such as schnitzel and knödel. For the best value, dine outside the immediate tourist centre.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Quick answers about Place of Silence – Hallstatt

items.q: Where is Place of Silence – Hallstatt located?
items.a: Place of Silence – Hallstatt is located at Gosaumühlstraße 67 along the lakeside road on the northern edge of Hallstatt, in Upper Austria, Austria. It is a short 5-10 minute walk north of the Market Square.
Follow current on-site signs and local instructions. This guide does not guarantee access at all times.
Keep noise low, respect private property and leave roads and entrances clear.

items.q: How do I get to the viewpoint from Salzburg?
items.a: For travel to Hallstatt, check current rail, bus and ferry connections with the operators and regional tourism office. Timetables, interchange points and service availability can change; the map here is for identification, not a dedicated photo-stop itinerary.

items.q: Is there parking near the viewpoint?
items.a: Use Hallstatt’s designated visitor parking and check current municipal access arrangements. Do not stop on the lakeside road or use residents’ entrances as parking or drop-off space.

items.q: Are there toilets, cafes or other facilities nearby?
items.a: The viewpoint itself has no facilities, but public toilets, cafes, restaurants and shops are a 5-10 minute walk away in the town centre, near the Market Square and the ferry landing.

items.q: How is this viewpoint different from the Skywalk?
items.a: Place of Silence is the lakeside place formerly referred to as Viewpoint. The Salzwelten Skywalk is a separate location above the town. This distinction is for identification and does not recommend either as an alternative photo itinerary; check current official information for the Skywalk.

officialManagement.title: About Place of Silence – Hallstatt
officialManagement.text: Place of Silence lies beside Hallstatt’s lakeside residential area.

facilities.title: On-site & Nearby Amenities
facilities.subtitle: The viewpoint is an open, unstaffed scenic overlook with no on-site facilities. The list below describes the general types of services found in Hallstatt and along the lakeside – for planning only.
facilities.note: For planning only – general service types, not a recommendation of any specific business. Availability and opening hours change with the seasons; please check locally.

items.detail: Free and paid public toilets are located along the lakeside promenade and near the boat / tourist jetties in Hallstatt.
Paid public parking areas at the southern entrance of Hallstatt (around Lahn) are the closest option for drivers; parking is not permitted in the historic centre.
Traditional restaurants, lakeside cafés and small snack bars line the promenade and the pedestrianised centre.
Hotels, guesthouses and holiday apartments are available in Hallstatt and in Obertraun on the opposite side of the lake.
A small supermarket as well as shops for groceries, drinks and souvenirs operate in the centre of Hallstatt.
Petrol stations and public charging points for electric cars are available in Obertraun and along the Salzkammergut road network.
Cash machines are available in Hallstatt centre; card payment is widely accepted in restaurants and shops.
The Hallstatt tourist information office provides maps, hiking routes and boat schedules for the lake area.

advice.outfitRain: Rain expected: wear a waterproof jacket or shoes and mind slippery ground.
advice.outfitSun: Clear skies: light clothes work well; keep a thin layer for the lakeside breeze.
advice.outfitSnow: Snowfall: warm winter coat and non-slip footwear.
advice.outfitUv: Strong UV – protect your skin and eyes.
advice.planSunny: Clear weather does not change the need for quiet and resident privacy. Follow local signs.
advice.planCloudy: Check conditions before walking; keep residential paths and entrances clear.
advice.planRainProb: High rain chance: keep outdoor plans flexible and have an indoor backup ready.
advice.planRainLight: Wet surfaces can be slippery. Follow local warnings and do not stop in the road.
advice.planNoOutdoor: Not a great day outdoors: boats/ferries and the salt-mine cable car may pause – favour indoor sights.
advice.planWind: Strong wind may change boat schedules; the viewpoint itself is exposed and cool.
advice.planHot: Avoid long outdoor hours around noon – early morning or evening is far more comfortable.
advice.planFog: Dense fog: the view is severely limited and ferries may run late.
advice.planSnow: Snowy day: footpaths and mountain trails can ice over; the cable car may pause at short notice.
advice.gearRaincoat: Raincoat (skip the long umbrella in wind)
advice.riskRainHeavy: Heavy rain: avoid stream valleys, gullies and low lakeside ground; watch your step on wet paths.
advice.riskThunder: Thunderstorms: do not stay on the open lakeside, summits or under trees – postpone the cable car and hikes.
advice.riskWind: Gale-force wind: keep away from jetties, billboards and loose objects; ferries/boats may suspend service.
advice.riskFog: Fog: poor visibility for driving and walking; ferries may be delayed.
